Read one passage of a document about machines at work (law, manual, guidance, internal guideline,
plant record) and write down the important facts it states.

Answer with one line per fact, fields separated by " | ", nothing else, no header, no code fence:
subject | predicate | object | condition | quote
- predicate: a short camelCase verb phrase of your choice.
- condition: any condition or exception, or "" if none.
- quote: the words of the passage the fact comes from.
At most 12 facts. If the passage states nothing important, answer with the single word NONE.

Passage: ur5e-manual, p. 229

21. Safety Functions Table 21. Safety Functions Table Description Universal Robots safety functions and safety I/O are PLd Category 3 (ISO 13849-1), where each safety function has a PFH value less than 1.8E-07. The PFH values are updated to include greater design flexibility for supply chain resilience. For safety I/O the resulting safety function including the external device, or equipment, is determined by the overall architecture and the sum of all PFHs, including the UR robot safety function PFH. If any safety function limit is exceeded or a fault is detected in a safety function or safety-related part of the control system, UR defines the safe state as a stop with removal of drive power (either a stop category 1 or 04 immediate removal of power). NOTICE The Safety Functions tables presented in this chapter are simplified. safe state on safety function limit exceeded or fault | isDefinedAs | stop with removal of drive power | safety function limit exceeded or fault detected | UR defines the safe state as a stop with removal of drive power
